sticky.title: Call 911 if you see:
tip.flames.title: Flames
tip.flames.body: Fire you can see outdoors, other than a campfire or fire pit someone is watching.
tip.column.title: Smoke column
tip.column.body: Smoke rising from one spot. Smoke from far away spreads out as haze; a column means the fire is close.
tip.dark.title: Dark smoke
tip.dark.body: Thick black or brown smoke. It often means a building, vehicle or dense brush is burning nearby.
check.tagline: Find out where the smoke is coming from, in 60 seconds.
check.replayNote: Replays Aug 25, 2025, during the Long Lake fire in Nova Scotia.
check.liveNote: Uses today’s fire, wind and air quality data.
q1.title: Do you see flames?
q2.title: What best describes it?
q2.hazeSub: The air looks hazy in every direction.
q2.smellSub: You smell smoke but can’t see where it comes from.
q2.column: Dark column rising from one spot
q2.columnSub: A plume of smoke going up from one place.

verdict.sub.unexplained: Look outside. If you see flames or a smoke column, call 911.

todo.title: What to do
advice.general.low: Ideal air quality for outdoor activities.
advice.general.moderate: No need to modify your usual outdoor activities unless you experience symptoms such as coughing and throat irritation.
advice.general.high: Consider reducing or rescheduling strenuous activities outdoors if you experience symptoms such as coughing and throat irritation.
advice.general.very_high: Reduce or reschedule strenuous activities outdoors, especially if you experience symptoms such as coughing and throat irritation.
advice.atRisk.moderate: Consider reducing or rescheduling strenuous activities outdoors if you are experiencing symptoms.
advice.atRisk.high: Reduce or reschedule strenuous activities outdoors. Children and the elderly should also take it easy.
advice.atRisk.very_high: Avoid strenuous activities outdoors. Children and the elderly should also avoid outdoor physical exertion.
todo.official.low: Official advice for an AQHI of {n} (low risk).
todo.official.moderate: Official advice for an AQHI of {n} (moderate risk).
todo.official.high: Official advice for an AQHI of {n} (high risk).
todo.official.very_high: Official advice for an AQHI of {n} (very high risk).
todo.nurse: Not an emergency but feeling unwell? Call 811 to talk to a nurse
todo.groups: Advice for people at higher risk
todo.higherRisk.list: seniors, children, pregnant people, people with heart or lung conditions, and people who work or exercise hard outdoors.
todo.doctor: People with heart or breathing problems: follow your doctor’s usual advice about exercise and managing your condition. Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada.
todo.noReading: No air quality reading from the last 2 hours.
aq.title: Air quality
aq.areaWide.text: Smoke from a nearby source can be much stronger where you are.
aq.source: Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada
why.title: Why we think this
why.traced: We traced the air back {n} hours
why.traced.body: Using hourly winds, we followed the air arriving in {town} backward, one hour at a time.
why.passed: It passed {km} km from an active fire
why.over: About {h} hours ago, that air was over {fire}.
why.over.one: About 1 hour ago, that air was over {fire}.
why.over.under: Less than an hour ago, that air was over {fire}.
why.seen: Satellites saw it burning in the last {n} hours.
why.seen.one: Satellites saw it burning in the last hour.
why.onList: It’s on Canada’s official active fire list.
why.closeButFar: Close, but farther than the {km} km we need to call it drifting smoke.
why.noneNear: No active fire near its path
why.noneNear.body: No fire within {km} km of any hourly step. The nearest, {nearest}, is {distance} km away and off the path.
why.noneInRegion: No active fires in the region
why.noneInRegion.body: No fires are reported within {km} km of you right now.
why.closeBy: The source may be close by
why.closeBy.body: A new fire, a brush pile burning, or wood smoke nearby may not show up in fire data yet.
why.steady.body: The wind direction barely changed along the way, so the traced path is more certain.
why.unsteady.overnight: An overnight wind shift makes the traced path less certain.
why.unsteady.body: A wind shift {when} makes the traced path less certain.
emergency.label: EMERGENCY
emergency.title: Call 911 now
emergency.sub: Flames or a smoke column can mean a fire near you.
emergency.tell1: address or nearest road and town
emergency.tell2: flames, a smoke column, or dark smoke
emergency.stay: Stay on the line and follow the dispatcher. If the fire is close to you, move away while you talk.
locationOff.title: Location is turned off
locationOff.sub: That’s fine. Search for your town instead.
locationOff.help: To use your location next time, allow it for this site in your browser or phone settings.
noData.label: NO VERDICT YET
noData.title: We can’t check the air right now
noData.sub: Fire or wind data isn’t loading, so we can’t tell you where this smoke is from.
noData.notNoFire: No verdict doesn’t mean no fire.
noData.lookOutside: Look outside. If you see flames or a smoke column, call 911.
how.title: How it works
how.intro: We look at where the air around you has been over the last day, and whether it passed a fire.
how.step1: You tell us where you are
how.step1.body: Share your location, or type your town.
how.step2.body: Using hourly wind data, we step the air arriving at your spot back in time, one hour per step.
how.step3: We check for fires along the way
how.step3.before: At every step we measure the
how.step3.after: : the shortest distance between the air and each active fire.
how.diagramAria: Diagram: the air’s hourly path passes a fire; the closest approach is the shortest distance between them
how.drifting.body: The air passed within 25 km of an active fire.
how.unclear.body: It passed 25 to 50 km from a fire, or the wind was unsteady.
how.unexplained.body: No active fire within 50 km of the air’s path.
how.aqhi: We add the Air Quality Health Index so you know what to do right now.
how.firms.body: Satellite fire detections (VIIRS and MODIS), some available less than a minute after the satellite passes over
how.limits.body: A fire that just started may not show up in satellite data for hours. If you see flames or a smoke column, call 911. Don’t wait for a verdict.
